question: Which filesystem policy contract should OpenClaw standardize on for this issue: PathGuard-style `allowedPaths`/`denyPaths`, `tools.fs.roots` with per-root access modes, or a broader security-profile model that also covers exec?
rationale: This defines a public config and local filesystem security boundary with competing open pull requests and an explicit exec-scope tradeoff, so automation should not choose the permanent contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Converge on `tools.fs` v1
options.body: Adopt one file/media/apply_patch policy model now, document or split exec scope, and require upgrade/security proof before merge.

options.title: Defer to security profile
options.body: Keep this issue as design input for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/8719 and avoid adding a narrow config surface until the broader data-security model is chosen.

options.title: Stay with workspace-only for now
options.body: Decline allow/deny or roots config for now and rely on `tools.fs.workspaceOnly`, tool allow/deny, Docker/OS isolation, and separate exec hardening work.

recommendation.title: Converge on `tools.fs` v1
recommendation.body: Adopt one file/media/apply_patch policy model now, document or split exec scope, and require upgrade/security proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest current-source and review-history signal for the config/security boundary decision.
